exposure: newborn hospitalization for more than 3 days
cohort: The study included 417 pregnant women and 388 lactating women participating in a Comprehensive Care Program in Bogota.
finding: Cesarean delivery, newborn hospitalization for more than 3 days, and lack of immediate skin-to-skin contact were identified as significant risk factors for immediate skin-to-skin contact and early initiation of breastfeeding.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was a significant risk factor for both lack of immediate skin-to-skin contact (OR: 23.15) and delayed early initiation of breastfeeding (OR: 2.6).
